We need to decide relation between two yes/no questions.

Q1: "O Brasil deve regular os mercados digitais inspirando-se nas experiências internacionais, como a Lei de Mercados Digitais da União Europeia?" This asks whether Brazil should regulate digital markets drawing on international experiences like EU DMA.

Q2: "A Câmara deve avançar na discussão e regulamentação dos mercados digitais (PL 2768/22)?" This asks whether the Chamber (Câmara) should advance discussion and regulation of digital markets (specific bill PL 2768/22).

Are they same issue? Both about regulating digital markets in Brazil. Q1 asks about Brazil regulating, inspired by EU DMA. Q2 asks about Câmara advancing discussion and regulation of digital markets (specific bill). The scope: Q1 is about Brazil (government) regulating, possibly via legislation; Q2 is about Câmara (legislative house) advancing discussion and regulation of a specific bill. They are related but not identical. The answer to Q1 (yes/no) does not necessarily determine answer to Q2. Could be yes to Brazil regulating but no to Câmara advancing that specific bill (maybe other path). Also Q1 mentions inspiration from EU DMA; Q2 doesn't mention that. So they are different questions, though same theme. So classification: DIFFERENT.

Reasoning: they address different actors and specific legislative proposal vs general policy. So answer DIFFERENT.
